page: UpCloud PREMIUM-48xCPU-256GB is an x86_64 compute-heavy instance powered by AMD EPYC 9575F processors running at 2.0 GHz on a KVM hypervisor. The virtual machine provision provides 48 physical cores mapping to 48 vCPUs with 1 thread per core under a shared CPU allocation model. Memory capacity totals 256.0 GB, yielding 5.33 GB of RAM per core. Hardware acceleration includes 500 GB of bundled local SSD storage and 1 complimentary public IPv4 address, while GPUs are absent. The processor incorporates vector instruction extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16, alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration with AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark results show top-tier computational capabilities. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 2,548.0 and a multi-core score of 23,628.0, placing both within the top 10 percent of recorded benchmarks. Clang software compilation reached 58,806.0, also placing it in the top 10 percent. Stress-ng scores reflect similar high performance, reaching 3,631.57 on single-core (top 10 percent) and 91,465.13 on multi-core testing (top 25 percent). PassMark overall CPU testing yielded 67,838.7 with strong results in cryptography, extended instruction sets, and database operations. Network serving throughput reached 52.75 GB/sec, accompanied by 68.18 million Redis SET operations per second.

The primary tradeoff centers on memory bandwidth and larger AI inferencing workloads. Cached memory reads perform in the top 25 percent at 5,450.04 GB/sec, but large-block uncached read and write bandwidths stabilize at average rates of 62.46 GB/sec and 63.91 GB/sec. Consequently, prompt processing on 7B parameter language models registers in the bottom 25 percent (17.86 tokens/sec), reflecting the absence of discrete GPU acceleration. The shared allocation profile offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for multithreaded compute. This configuration is best suited for continuous integration, Clang software builds, distributed database nodes, Redis caching layers, and high-concurrency static web serving.
description: UpCloud PREMIUM-48xCPU-256GB is an x86_64 cloud instance configured with 48 AMD EPYC 9575F vCPUs at 2.0 GHz, 256.0 GB of system RAM, and 500 GB of bundled local SSD storage. Delivering 5.33 GB of memory per core without discrete GPUs, it features advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and cryptographic offloading. Benchmark results place its single-core and multi-core processing power in the top tier, scoring 2,548.0 and 23,628.0 in Geekbench respectively, with top-tier performance in Clang software compilation. Cached read speeds reach 5,450.04 GB/sec, while static web throughput hits 52.75 GB/sec. Uncached large-block memory transfers and medium LLM inference show average-to-weak rates due to standard memory pathways and lack of accelerators. Given its dense multithreading capacity and qualitative compute efficiency, it is well fitted for compilation pipelines, web serving clusters, large Redis in-memory caches, and database backends.
